newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Yeltsin leaves for Germany.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Yeltsin leaves for Germany.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin left for Germany on Wednesday for a two-day visit which includes talks with his friend, Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Itar-Tass news agency said.

The talks between the two leaders, their second meeting in just three months, are likely to focus on intensive efforts to negotiate a charter defining Russia's relationship with the expanding NATO defence alliance.
The two leaders will also discuss bilateral economic ties. Germany is Russia's biggest financial backer.
On Tuesday, Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana apparently failed in Moscow talks to resolve remaining differences over NATO plans to expand eastwards.
Relations between Russia and Germany have been complicated by the Russian parliament's refusal to allow the return of art treasures seized by the Red Army from the Nazis.
The upper chamber of parliament is to debate the issue on Wednesday, considering whether to back the lower house in overruling Yeltsin's veto of a draft law which says the art should stay in Russia.
Kohl told Tass on Monday he was confident about "personal trust and friendship" with Yeltsin and confident that Russia's dispute with NATO would be settled satisfactorily.

The Russian president will receive a "Man of the Year" award from the German media in the spa resort of Baden-Baden, a title previously won by late French president Francois Mitterrand, late Israeli premier Yitzhak Rabin and by Kohl himself.
Yeltsin, 66, will fly to Stuttgart and travel by road to Baden-Baden with his wife Naina and, for the first time in a such a public role abroad, his younger daughter, Tatyana Dyachenko, 37.
